findings.cross_file_justification: The newly declared review-catch-only arms enter ablation-report.py's components list, but its unchanged primaries() requires both hidden_test_pass_rate and defect_catch_rate for these arms.
findings.description: The new review-only components cannot reach a decidable remove/simplify outcome. Their task_types prohibit build trials, so hidden_test_pass_rate can never have a valid pair.
findings.failure_mode: Even with sufficient admissible review trials demonstrating equivalence, the report falls back to 'inconclusive: no valid pair (hidden_test_pass_rate)' and marks the component undecidable.
findings.suggested_fix: Select primary metrics according to the arm's applicable task types: require defect_catch_rate for review-catch-only arms and hidden_test_pass_rate only for arms applicable to build tasks.

findings.description: Excluding eval_only arms from components also removes their valid results from the report. The open-mount arm is not included in detail_arms, and list_reason does not classify its otherwise admissible rows as excluded.
findings.failure_mode: A batch can successfully run the open-mount oracle control, yet its valid measurements disappear from the report, preventing the intended open-versus-closed evaluation comparison.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep eval_only arms excluded from decisions and the component count, but include them in descriptive result tables and JSON output with their evaluation-only designation.

findings.cross_file_justification: The diff adds the first review-catch-only arms (a0_bare_fable, a1_review_only, a1_no_dissent at evals/suites/ablation-2.0.yaml:98-103) and the new components expression at head:1913 admits them as decision components. The unchanged primaries() (head:653-658) returns [hidden_test_pass_rate, defect_catch_rate] for any arm whose task_types contains review-catch, so the decision path for these arms depends on a metric they can never produce.
findings.description: Review-catch-only arms are counted as components, but the decision machinery still requires a hidden_test_pass_rate pair for them. Those arms have no build rows, so compare(PASS) never pairs, usable() is false and decide() falls to 'inconclusive: no valid pair (hidden_test_pass_rate)' regardless of how many review-catch rows exist. remove/simplify is unreachable and decidable is always False for the three new arms. The test change in ablation-report.bats only asserts the decision count (9), not the decision content, so this is not caught.
findings.failure_mode: Every batch report emits a permanently inconclusive decision for a0_bare_fable, a1_review_only and a1_no_dissent, no matter how much review-catch data is collected; the expected-false-positive line also counts them in k, so the stated error budget overstates the number of real tests.
findings.suggested_fix: Make primaries() derive from the arm's task_types: review-catch-only arms get [defect_catch_rate] alone (build-only arms already get [hidden_test_pass_rate]); add a bats assertion that a review-catch-only arm with a valid CATCH pair reaches a non-inconclusive decision.

findings.cross_file_justification: The diff excludes eval_only arms from components (head:1913) and the suite declares a1_full_openmount eval_only (ablation-2.0.yaml:104-105). The report's other arm-rendering paths (list_reason, detail_arms, the Decisions and Exclusions tables) key off components/absent only, so the eval_only arm is in neither set.
findings.description: The comment calls the eval_only arm 'an evaluation control' (the open-mount vs closed-mount oracle A/B), yet after this change its rows are not decided, not listed and not rendered anywhere: it is not a component, not CONTROL/BARE and not absent, and list_reason returns None for a present arm that applies to review-catch. Only its excluded rows surface, in the Exclusions table. The A/B the arm exists to provide cannot be read from the report at all.
findings.failure_mode: Valid a1_full_openmount rows silently disappear from report.md and report.json; operators spend review-catch trials on the open-mount arm and the FR-5 oracle comparison is never surfaced, with no warning that rows were dropped.
findings.suggested_fix: Give eval_only arms an explicit rendering path: an 'Evaluation controls' section that reports defect_catch_rate for the arm against CONTROL (a1_full) with its interval, excluded from Decisions and from k. Add a bats case asserting that an eval_only arm's valid rows appear in that section and that no valid row is unaccounted for across Decisions, Evaluation controls and Exclusions.

findings.cross_file_justification: The suite adds a0_bare_fable (a bare baseline on the review model); the components expression at ablation-report.py:1913 only excludes the ids named by CONTROL and BARE, so this second bare baseline becomes a component.
findings.description: a0_bare_fable is a baseline arm (no mount, bare model), the review-catch analogue of a0_bare, but it is treated as a component whose decision vocabulary is remove/simplify/investigate/keep relative to a1_full. Removing or simplifying a baseline is meaningless, and it inflates k in the expected-false-positive line.
findings.failure_mode: The Decisions table carries a nonsense decision row for a baseline arm and the error-budget sentence counts a non-test as a test.
findings.suggested_fix: Mark baseline arms in the suite (e.g. `role: baseline`) or extend the BARE exclusion to any arm with toggles.loa_mount == false, and render such arms as baselines rather than components.

findings.cross_file_justification: The efp_line now says 'over 9 components' while the suite rules block (ablation-2.0.yaml head:117, unchanged) still reads 'over 6 components'; AR-12 asserts the Method section quotes the rules block verbatim, so both statements land in the same report.
findings.description: The report will state two different component counts: 9 in the computed sentence and 6 in the verbatim rules block.
findings.failure_mode: Self-contradictory Method section; readers cannot tell which error budget applies.
findings.suggested_fix: Update the rules block in ablation-2.0.yaml to the new count or, better, remove the hard-coded number from the rules text and let the computed sentence be the single source.

findings.description: TOGGLE_VALUES in validate-suite.sh and the sb_edits jq in pipeline-run.sh's dry run (head:342-346) are both hand copies of lib/sandbox-mount.sh apply_arm_toggles: the toggle vocabulary and the toggle→.loa.config.yaml edit mapping. RULE_IDS is correctly read from took-effect.sh, but the toggle vocabulary is not read from the lib even though validate-suite.sh already sources it. There is no parity test; the new bats cases only compare against literal strings.
findings.failure_mode: A toggle added or renamed in apply_arm_toggles is silently rejected by the validator (or an edit the lib makes is missing from the dry-run plan) until someone notices the mismatch by hand.
findings.suggested_fix: Export the vocabulary from lib/sandbox-mount.sh (e.g. a TOGGLE_VOCAB associative array or a `toggle_vocabulary` function printing key=value lines) and consume it in both validate-suite.sh and the dry run; add a bats test that applies each toggle via apply_arm_toggles to a scratch config and asserts the resulting key set equals the dry-run config_edits list.

findings.cross_file_justification: The suite names five new rule ids (oracle_closed, oracle_open_recorded, bare_model_fable, review_only_phases, no_review_dissent_envelope) and the validator now rejects any id without a matching `rule_<id>() {` in took-effect.sh, which is not part of this diff.
findings.description: RULE_IDS is extracted with a sed pattern that only matches `rule_<id>() {` definitions on one line. took-effect.sh is not in the diff, so it cannot be confirmed here that all five new rule functions exist in that exact form. If any is missing or declared differently (`function rule_x`, brace on the next line), the committed suite fails validation.
findings.failure_mode: validate-suite.sh exits 1 on the committed suite (VS-14 and VS-16 fail), blocking every batch that runs the validator pre-flight.
findings.suggested_fix: Confirm took-effect.sh in the same PR defines all five rules with the `rule_<id>() {` shape, and consider having took-effect.sh expose a `--list-rules` mode the validator calls instead of parsing source text.
